entry_conditions: Accept the full demonstrated expanded entry, not just a blue-in-hand state. At the earliest supported entry, world-frame drawer position d is about 0.300 m, red center z about 0.211 m over the outside pad, TCP is about 9 mm to the negative-world-x side of red at similar height, measured total finger width qpos[7]+qpos[8] is about 0.03649 m, and blue is still at its outside source near z=0.020 m. Also accept later shared red-release, open-finger retreat/blue-approach, blue closure and initial-lift states. Use both causal observations, joint velocities, TCP/red/blue poses (wxyz), finger positions and drawer position/velocity to infer the current transition and apparent object coupling. These are observed support descriptions, not hard geometric admission thresholds or proof of contact. Source blue XY varies across demonstrations.
exit_conditions: No mandatory successor. The task monitor may stop at the first actual observation satisfying all supplied goals: d>0.26 m, red fully on the pad centered at (-0.18,-0.30) with half widths (0.06,0.06) and 0.014<red_z<0.031, and blue fully inside the drawer centered in XY at (0.19-d,0) with half widths (0.172,0.182) and 0.053<blue_z<0.074. Full XY containment includes rotated cube extents e_i=0.02*sum_j(abs(R_ij)). Predicted success is not sufficient. Closed fingers do not invalidate actual completion: demo1000:980 already has blue z about 0.067 m and valid concurrent goals. If continued, a demonstrated useful exit has red z about 0.020 m, blue z about 0.063 m, d about 0.2974 m, open fingers totaling about 0.080 m and TCP z about 0.323 m. This high-TCP exit is optional, not an added success requirement.
overlap_role: This model learns actual red lowering/placement/release and blue acquisition as well as transport/insertion; it must preserve red and the open drawer rather than force immediate blue containment in the prerequisite prefix. The measured overlap with evacuate_red spans 270-278 actions per demonstration, beginning at red z about 0.211 m and extending to blue initial lift. In demo1000, red is still slightly above the pad height band at 595 and 605, releases by 615, and remains on the pad during open-finger retreat at 640. Blue is close to the TCP with narrow fingers at 815 and rises together with it through 844-845. A handoff partway through this transition needs no elapsed-time index: causal object/TCP separation and displacement, finger aperture, qpos/qvel and achieved-goal geometry condition the learned model. Red already on the pad alone does not identify whether blue approach, grasp or lift is underway.
successor_readiness: There is no required next manipulation skill. If the task is not complete, continue this model within demonstrated support while it completes the relevant transition; red-on-pad alone is not the whole-task endpoint. If transferring after actual simultaneous success, communicate measured d, both object poses, current finger opening and TCP-object separation/motion so a successor can preserve the achieved conjunction. For a clearance-oriented continuation, the retained terminal support provides open fingers and a TCP well above the blue object. This optional readiness description never overrides the one-observation completion rule.
failure_signatures: Escalate to the task-level agent rather than claiming trained recovery if actual blue fails to move with the TCP after closure/lift, predicted or implied insertion progress disagrees with measured blue remaining outside, red leaves its pad during blue travel, d declines toward 0.26 m, or action chunks produce unsupported pauses or unnatural commands. Finger narrowing and co-motion only suggest a grasp; there are no force/contact observations. Ensemble disagreement is a training-time conservative scoring term, not a calibrated deployment safety alarm, and the fixed deployment forward does not run the ensemble.
continuation_guidance: Reobserve after the fixed short action prefix (8 execution steps) and decide from actual state. During red lowering, finish the demonstrated placement/release before blue acquisition; with open fingers and red on the pad, distinguish retreat/approach by TCP trajectory relative to blue. With blue close to the TCP, narrow fingers and upward object motion, continue supported lift/transport/lowering while preserving red and d. Once the actual conjunction holds, stopping is permitted even before release; if choosing to continue, use only demonstrated-like release/retreat while monitoring goal preservation. Do not require a dwell, low velocity, particular final joint pose or TCP clearance to declare success. The policy is a learned diffusion model, not a phase-scripted controller.
limitations: Boundary and overlap measurements establish training support, not learned-policy success. Off-manifold lost-grasp recovery, rim collision avoidance and counterfactual action ranking are unproven. The fixed epsilon-only sampler interface required amortized training-time lookahead selection instead of runtime multi-chunk reranking. The causal progress head estimates local future geometric work, not remaining task duration. No images, IK, analytic manipulator kinematics, collision/force model, calibrated uncertainty or guaranteed action equivariance are implemented. All normalization is the shared full-demonstration normalization; this skill does not refit scales.
